name: τ²-Bench Airline
description: The airline domain split of τ²-bench (tau2-bench), evaluating conversational agents in a dual-control environment where both the AI agent and the user can independently invoke tools. Modeled as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP), the agent must coordinate with a simulated user to complete airline customer service tasks (bookings, modifications, cancellations, refunds) while adhering to domain policies.
evaluation_method: pass^k (task success reliability across k repeated attempts); task completion rate
general_score_metric: pass^k (task success reliability); task completion rate
typical_sota_score: Frontier models achieve 40–65% task completion on airline domain; dual-control significantly harder than single-agent τ-bench
reputation: Princeton University 2025; extends τ-bench to dual-control Dec-POMDP setting; airline domain is one of three canonical splits alongside retail and telecom; exposes new coordination and communication failure modes
notes: arXiv:2506.07982 (2025). τ²-bench extends the original τ-bench by introducing a dual-control environment (Dec-POMDP): both the agent and user can take tool actions, requiring explicit coordination and communication. Airline domain covers flight booking, itinerary changes, cancellations, and refunds. HuggingFace: HuggingFaceH4/tau2-bench-data. Official repo: github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench.
